false-logotype-branding-exemption: Real logos may be pictures of text, but authors abuse this by saving taglines, slogans, or headings as images so low-vision users can't resize or recolour them.
customizability-exception-onpage-control: A picture of text is allowed if on-page controls truly let users adjust its size, font, and colour, but those controls are sometimes fake, broken, or change nothing.
significant-other-visual-content-exclusi: Charts, screenshots, and diagrams that contain words are exempt, so judging whether an image is mostly-graphic (allowed) or just styled text (not allowed) needs a human.
in-addition-to-equivalent-live-text: A picture of text is fine when the exact same words also appear as real visible text nearby, but checkers can't confirm the live text truly matches.
essential-presentation-beyond-logos: Some pictures of text are allowed because their exact look matters (a font sample, a scanned historical letter), and judging whether the look is essential needs a human.
image-of-text-vs-live-text-core-detectio: Words baked into images (CSS backgrounds, SVG, sprites) instead of real text can't be resized or recoloured, and tools often can't even detect that the image contains text.
